footer.safeBadge: 🛡️ Search Intermediary Provider • Zero Local Storage of Files
footer.disclaimerText: Intermediary & Liability Disclaimer: Lino Livre strictly operates as an intermediary search index for publicly available external hyperlinks. Our servers and database do not store or host binary book files (PDF, EPUB, TXT). All reading access occurs via protocol redirects (HTTP 302). Rightsholders may request immediate link removal via bv6alblu6@mozmail.com.

synopses.1: Bento Santiago's first-person account of his youth, his childhood love for Capitu and his doubts about marital fidelity.
synopses.2: A revolutionary work narrated by a deceased author, introducing realism in Brazil with irony and psychological genius.

synopses.5: The tragicomic portrait of an idealistic patriot who proposes tupi-guarani as Brazil's official language and faces the country's contradictions.
synopses.6: A collection bringing together The Slave Ship and other famous poems by Castro Alves, the peak of Brazilian lyric and abolitionist poetry.
synopses.7: The legend of Ceará and the founding romance between the honey-lipped virgin and the white warrior Martim.

synopses.36: First book by an Angolan author printed in Angola (1849). Lyric and nostalgic poetry by José da Silva Maia Ferreira, born in Luanda.
synopses.37: Complete poetry of Alda Lara, pioneering Angolan poetess (1904–1930). Themes of love, land, identity and social justice in free verse.
synopses.38: Poems by Viriato da Cruz (1928–1967), greatest 20th-century Angolan poet. Founding voice of intervention and liberation poetry in Angola.
synopses.39: Novel by José Eduardo Agualusa (2012). Portuguese woman isolates herself in Luanda for 30 years; diary, poems and reflections on independent Angola. Dublin Award 2017.
synopses.40: Novel by Pepetela (1980). Liberation war in Mayombe: guerrillas of various ethnicities build Angolan national unity in practice.
synopses.41: Novel by Pepetela (1992). Trajectory of a generation of Angolan nationalists from armed struggle to power, confronting utopias and realities.
synopses.42: Novel by Ondjaki (2012). Contemporary Luanda: corruption, oil, memory and survival. José Saramago Prize 2013.
synopses.43: Novel by Boaventura Cardoso (2001). Angolan mother faces war, loss and memory. Deep reflection on motherhood and resistance.
synopses.44: Collection by José Luandino Vieira (2004). Tales from Luanda's musseque: daily life, cultural resistance and reinvented Portuguese.
synopses.45: Work by Uanhenga Xitu (1984). Cokwe oral tradition transcribed: Master Tamoda teaches wisdom, ethics and Angolan people's history.
synopses.46: Poetry by Agostinho Neto (1974). Angola's first president: verses of struggle, hope and nation-building. Includes 'Sagrada Esperança'.
synopses.47: Novel by Ondjaki (2003). Childhood in post-independence Luanda: dreams, games and discovery of the adult world. Jabuti Juvenile Prize.
synopses.48: Novel by Mia Couto (1992). Mozambique at war: two men — an old storyteller, a boy — travel devastated roads. Camões Prize 2013.
synopses.49: Poetry by José Craveirinha (2004). Greatest Mozambican poet: verses of prison, resistance and African identity in reinvented Portuguese.
synopses.50: Novel by Baltasar Lopes (1947). Cape Verde: Chiquinho grows up between drought, emigration and awakening Creole consciousness. Lusophone classic.
synopses.51: Poetry by Corsino Fortes (1986). Cape Verde: tree and drum, identity and diaspora. Camões Prize 1989 (first African).
synopses.52: Poetry by Jorge Barbosa (1941). Cape Verde: clarity, sea and saudade. Founder of Claridade Review, milestone of Cape Verdean modernism.
synopses.53: Novel by Fernando Monteiro de Castro Soromenho (1961). Colonial Angola: drought, famine and tragedy of forced railway workers.
synopses.54: Novel by Dina Salústio (2009). Cape Verde: women, tradition and modernity. First Cape Verdean woman to publish a novel. Camões Prize 2020.
synopses.55: Novel by Germano Almeida (2018). Cape Verde: mystery, humour and social critique. Camões Prize 2018.
